title: Enterprise data-controls triage rubric & routing playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a practical, prescriptive triage rubric and routing playbook for non-bug customer requests related to data governance controls (logging redaction, log retention, PII handling, audit exports). Goal: reduce time-to-first-response, ensure correct escalation to Legal/Security/Infra, and provide deterministic routing for Dedicated/Private customers with compliance needs.
decision_rubric: Primary axes: regulatory scope (GDPR/CCPA/sector-specific), data sensitivity (PII/PHI/low), number of affected customers, required retention change (temporary vs policy-level), engineering effort estimate (hrs), and operational risk (rollback complexity).
Urgency mapping: legal subpoena or regulator inquiry -> P0 and immediate Escalate to Dir of Security; contractual breach -> P0/QSLA; standard policy change -> P2.

Routing priorities: Legal (for regulatory/contractual), Security (for PII/PHI handling), Infra/Runtime (for retention policy and KV-cache/ingest changes), Console/Support (for customer comms and SLAs).
Fallback behavior: If infra change >24h and customer is high-revenue, engage temporary compensating controls (access restrictions, custom retention policy) and assign a dedicated PM/SE liaison.
intake_form_fields: Request type: {logging_redaction, retention_change, pii_masking, audit_export, other}
Affected product(s) and deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
Is there an active contract clause or legal hold? (yes/no)
Business impact estimate (low/medium/high) and monthly spend tier
Attachments (policy doc, legal notice, sample logs)
triage_flow_summary: 1) Intake form submitted -> automated label assignment in Zendesk/Support ticketing -> Linear PM queue (data-controls).
2) PM performs quick triage (<= 4 business hours): validate completeness, classify by decision rubric, and assign owner(s).
3) For Legal/Security classification: immediate 1:1 with Security lead and Legal SME; for Infra work: create ENG ticket with priority mapping and retention/rollback plan.
4) Communicate expected SLA to customer within 8 business hours with next steps and temporary mitigations if applicable.
5) Track full lifecycle in Linear with tags: triaged_by_pm, security_reviewed, infra_work_created, customer_committed.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence playbook published with decision rubric and example mappings (at least 6 realistic example requests).
Intake form template created and wired into Support (Zendesk flow) and Linear auto-labeling rule tested end-to-end.
Routing matrix defined and signed off by Legal, Security, and Head of Infra.
Two-week pilot with top-10 enterprise customers: record SLA adherence and <24h first meaningful response for high-impact requests.
Automation: at least 3 label-based workflows (legal escalation, infra ticket creation, security consult) deployed and verified.
notes_and_considerations: Private deployments often require customer-managed KMS and local retention enforcement; plan for a different routing path and a longer lead time.
For Dedicated customers, coordinate with Account Execs early; some customers may require contract amendments rather than ad-hoc changes.
Any change touching raw logs -> mandatory Security sign-off and short threat-modeling checklist before infra work begins.
Design should provide a concise console notice pattern and email template for customers describing what changed and the revert plan.
